red_flags: Did not send a brief acknowledgement to the landlord (the human did, but it is optional)
Did not assign a contractor, although the human operator did so at once; the agent's tool results showed none on record
Added a profile fact about 'Felix' based on an assumption that he is the landlord's partner
reasoning: The landlord's reply approves a contractor looking at the window. The agent correctly read it as approval. 'When convenient' only affects timing, and no cost was committed. It recorded the approval, moved the ticket to provider selection and told the tenant a contractor is being arranged. It then escalated contractor selection to ops, because no contractor was on record, and set a hold. This matches the human's path: approval confirmed, then provider selection. The agent did not invent a contractor. The tenant message was not marked as claiming anything unverified. It also stated that any quote would go back to the landlord. Minor weaknesses: no acknowledgement to the landlord, which is optional, and the 'Felix' fact rests on an assumption. The agent also did not assign a provider itself, but with no contractor on record, escalating was reasonable.
